sentences.text: Hello, everyone.
My name is Emily.
Today, we are going to learn how to speak English
at the airport.
Airports can be big, crowded, and confusing.
Many people speak English at airports,
but sometimes it is difficult to understand.
Don't worry, in this episode, I will teach you.
One, how to check in for your flight.
Two, how to go through security.
Three, how to ask for help at the airport.
Four, how to find your gate and wait for your flight.
Five, how to board the plane.
Six, how to go through immigration and customs
when you arrive.
I will also give you useful words and phrases to help you.
Are you ready?
Let's begin checking in for your flight.
When you arrive at the airport, the first step is check in.
You need to go to the airline check-in counter or kiosk.
The airline staff will say, hello,
can I see your passport, please?
Which airline are you flying with?
You can reply, yes, here you go.
Give your passport, I'm flying with British Airways.
Then they will ask, do you have any luggage to check in?
How many bags do you have?
Thus you can say, yes, I have one suitcase.
No, I only have a carry-on bag.
If your suitcase is too heavy, they will say,
your bag is overweight, you need to pay extra.
Now the airline staff will give you your boarding pass.
They will say, here is your boarding pass.
Your gate number is B12.
Your flight boards at 10.30 a.m.
You can say, thank you.
Now you are ready to go to security.
Going through security.
At security, you must show your passport and boarding pass.
The security officer may say,
please place your bag on the conveyor belt.
Take off your jacket and shoes.
Do you have any liquids?
You can ask, do I need to take out my laptop?
Can I bring water?
Remember, you cannot bring large bottles of water.
You must take out your laptop and liquids.
If everything is okay, the security officer will say,
you can go through.
Now you are in the airport terminal,
finding your gate and waiting for your flight.
After security, you need to find your gate.
You can look at the departure board or ask for help.
You can ask, excuse me, where is gate B12?
How do I get to terminal three?
If your flight is delayed, the board will say,
delayed until 11.45 a.m.
If your flight is canceled,
you need to go to the airline desk and say,
excuse me, my flight is canceled.
What should I do?
While you wait, you can sit in the waiting area.
Go to a cafe and get coffee.
Go shopping at duty-free stores.
Ask your boarding the plane.
When it is time to board, the staff will say,
now boarding flight one, two, three to London.
Passengers in group A, please board now.
You give them your boarding pass and say,
here you go.
They will check your ticket and say,
enjoy your flight.
Now you walk onto the plane and find your seat.
If you need help, you can ask,
excuse me, where is seat 12A?
On the plane, when you find your seat,
you put your carry-on bag in the overhead bin.
The flight attendant will say,
please fasten your seat belt.
Please turn off your phone.
During the flight, you can ask for something.
Can I have some water, please?
Do you have a vegetarian meal?
If you feel sick, you can say,
excuse me, I don't feel well.
After a few hours, the captain will say,
we are now landing.
Now you have arrived.
Arriving at your destination.
When you arrive at the airport,
you go through immigration.
The immigration officer will ask,
can I see your passport?
What is the purpose of your visit?
You can answer, I am here for tourism.
I am here for business.
Then you go to baggage claim to get your suitcase.
If you cannot find your luggage, you can ask.
Excuse me, my bag is missing.
What should I do?
Finally, you go through customs.
If you have nothing to declare,
you can walk through the green lane.
Now, you are in a new country.
Useful airport vocabulary.
Here are some important words and phrases to remember.
Airport phrases.
Can I see your passport?
Do you have any luggage to check in?
Where is my gate?
Is my flight on time?
Can I have a window seat?
Enjoy your flight.
Where is baggage claim?
Common airport words.
Check encounter where you check in for your flight.
Boarding pass.
Your ticket to enter the plane.
Gate.
The place where you wait to get on the plane.
Security check.
Where staff check your bags.
Carry on bag.
A small bag you take on the plane.
Suitcase.
A big bag for clothes.
Flight attendant.
A person who helps you on the plane.
Arrival.
When a plane lands.
Departure.
When a plane leaves.
Now you know how to speak English at the airport.
Practice these phrases before you travel.
